item.text: {"text":"Recent work separates explanation plausibility, factual grounding, and model faithfulness. RecSys 2024’s [LLMs as Evaluators for Recommendation Explanations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.03248) compares automated judgments with user feedback and third-party annotations; results depend on prompts and evaluation settings. [Walk the Talk? (ICLR 2025)](https://www.media.mit.edu/publications/walk-the-talk-llm-faithfulness/) measures whether concepts cited in explanations actually influence predictions through counterfactual interventions. Implication: title/description agreement establishes textual support, not why SASRec recommended an item. Broad thematic associations should therefore remain weak evidence rather than validated explanations.\n\nA practical diagnostic taxonomy—an adaptation, not an established taxonomy from these papers—would distinguish: explicit contradiction supported by quoted metadata; near-duplicate exposure supported by matching identifiers or substantial title/description overlap; weak task support where only broad topical similarity exists; and insufficient information where required attributes are absent. Record evidence spans and the specific inferred task; history alone cannot establish current ownership, dissatisfaction, or device compatibility. Abstain on those claims unless explicitly supported. [Know Your Limits (TACL 2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.tacl-1.26/) surveys abstention as a reliability mechanism. Before trusting automated counts, independently double-annotate a category-balanced sample, report per-label agreement and Cohen’s kappa or Krippendorff’s alpha, adjudicate disagreements, and measure abstention coverage separately. Keep these diagnostics distinct from validation HR@10; exclude unavailable reviews, ratings, simulator traits, and external pretrained weights."}
